stem: Why should a technician use a consistent scouting route?
choices: It reduces observation bias and makes repeated scouting rounds easier to compare
It ensures every plant receives identical attention, so differences in pest distribution become less important during interpretation
It allows the route to be shortened when pressure appears low without affecting the comparability of later scouting records
It lets the technician focus mainly on previously affected plants while still treating the results as representative of the entire room
rationale: Repeatable routes and inspection methods make trends and changes easier to detect and reduce bias toward only obvious problem areas.
